eyebrow: The gap standard tokens leave open
code:
# 9:00am  user signs in, gets an access token (~1hr lifetime)
# 9:05am  admin disables the account - it's been compromised
#
# standard OAuth: the token the attacker holds is still honored
#                 by the resource provider until it expires
#
# "verify explicitly" at sign-in only is a snapshot, not continuous
caption: A token issued once is normally honored for its full lifetime, no matter what changes after.

eyebrow: What CAE pushes, in near real time

steps.label: Account disabled or deleted
steps.sub: resource provider stops honoring the token almost immediately

steps.label: Password changed, or tokens explicitly revoked
steps.sub: an admin-initiated reset propagates right away

steps.label: User risk evaluated as high
steps.sub: Identity Protection signals like impossible travel trigger revocation

code:
# login-time check (Conditional Access at sign-in):
#   "was this request trustworthy WHEN it was made?"
#
# continuous evaluation (CAE, throughout the session):
#   "is this session STILL trustworthy right now?"
#
# zero trust needs both answered - not just the first one
caption: A session legitimate at 9:00am can become illegitimate minutes later.
